strengths: Principled and well-motivated approach: The core insight of coordinating positional encoding extrapolation with the spectral progression of the diffusion process (where low frequencies solidify early and high frequencies evolve throughout) is theoretically grounded and supported by empirical Fourier analysis.
Training-free and zero-overhead: DyPE operates purely at inference time without requiring parameter fine-tuning, architecture modification, or additional sampling steps.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Experiments span multiple state-of-the-art diffusion transformers (FLUX, FiTv2, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1), varied resolutions up to 4096×4096 (16M+ pixels), multiple tasks (text-to-image, class-conditional, video generation, image editing, panorama synthesis), and extensive comparison against both PE-based baselines (PI, NTK-aware, YaRN, TASR) and general high-resolution pipelines (HiFlow, DemoFusion, Diffusion-4K).

Rigorous ablations and analyses: The manuscript provides insightful ablation studies comparing scheduler dynamics (multiplicative vs. exponential, scheduler powers), clear contrast against contrary prior methods like TASR (Lumina-Next), and attention entropy analysis confirming preservation of native attention profiles.
weaknesses: Computational and memory footprint at test time: While training-free, running full self-attention at 4096×4096 still incurs significant memory and compute costs due to quadratic attention scaling in sequence length. The paper would benefit from reporting inference time and peak VRAM usage across resolutions compared to patch-based or cascaded methods.

Statistical reliability of FID on small datasets: On Aesthetic-4K, the FID metric is computed over a subset of only 195 image-prompt pairs; standard FID estimators are known to suffer high bias and variance at such small sample sizes.

Minor formatting and text artifacts: On page 18, under the Appendix qualitative headers, there is a stray typographical artifact (an isolated letter 'e' between paragraphs), indicating minor polishing is needed in the supplementary sections.

Sensitivity to noise schedules and samplers: The theoretical derivations in Sec. 3.1 explicitly leverage the linear schedule of Flow Matching. A clearer discussion on how the optimal scheduler parameters (e.g., $\lambda_s, \lambda_t$) translate across different diffusion schedules (e.g., VP-SDE, cosine schedules) would further strengthen the work.

strengths: Principled and intuitive motivation: The paper provides a clear Fourier-space analysis of the diffusion generation process, showing that low-frequency global structures converge early while high-frequency details evolve throughout sampling. This justifies dynamic, time-dependent positional extrapolation over static LLM-derived schemes.

Training-free and efficient: DyPE is entirely training-free and introduces zero additional parameter or inference computational overhead, making it practical to integrate directly into existing pre-trained DiTs.

Comprehensive empirical validation: The method is extensively tested on text-to-image models (FLUX at resolutions up to 4096x4096 and 6144x6144, Qwen-Image), class-conditional synthesis (FiTv2 on ImageNet), video diffusion (Wan2.1 on VBench), image editing, and panorama generation.

Thorough evaluation: The experimental setup covers standard automatic metrics (CLIP-Score, ImageReward, Aesthetic Score, FID, patch-FID, IS), a 50-rater human evaluation study with decisive win rates (70.5%-94.2%), and attention entropy analysis explaining the mechanism's stability.
weaknesses: Heuristic scheduler formulation: While the spectral progression analysis in Section 3.1 is mathematically well-founded, the proposed dynamic scaling schedule $\kappa(t) = \lambda_s \cdot t^{\lambda_t}$ remains heuristic rather than directly derived in closed form from the progression index $\gamma(f, t)$.

Hardware and memory practicalities at extreme resolutions: Although DyPE adds no extra algorithmic overhead, running full DiT self-attention at 4096x4096 involves 16x token count and substantial memory footprints. The paper states that single L40S GPUs (48GB) were used, but details on how full-sequence attention was managed (e.g., memory optimizations, FlashAttention variants, or sequence chunking) should be explicitly documented.

strengths: Principled and theoretically grounded motivation: The paper provides a clean Fourier-domain spectral analysis of the flow matching reverse process ($x_t = (1-t)x + t\epsilon$), formally showing that low-frequency components solidify early in sampling while high frequencies evolve continuously towards $t \to 0$.

Simple, elegant, and training-free method: By introducing a simple time-dependent decay scheduler $\kappa(t) = \lambda_s t^{\lambda_t}$ into position extrapolation techniques (PI, NTK-aware, YaRN), DYPE dynamically transitions from structural context scaling at early steps to native, uncompressed high-frequency RoPE representations at late steps, incurring zero additional inference compute or memory overhead.

Comprehensive empirical validation across models and modalities: The method is validated thoroughly on FLUX.1 (T2I), FiTv2 (ImageNet class-conditional), Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit (multi-concept editing), and Wan2.1 (video generation), demonstrating broad applicability across modern diffusion transformers utilizing RoPE.

Rigorous evaluation: The paper includes diverse automated metrics (FID, patch-FID, Inception Score, patch-IS, CLIP score, ImageReward, Aesthetics Score), user studies with 50 raters, resolution stress-testing up to $6144^2$, ablation studies on scheduler parametrizations, and an insightful attention entropy deviation analysis.

Clear differentiation from prior art: The authors contrast their formulation with Time-Aware Scaled RoPE (TASR / Lumina-Next), explaining why TASR's transition (interpolating towards NTK-aware) suppresses high frequencies compared to DYPE's relaxation back to uncompressed native coordinates, supported by direct head-to-head empirical comparisons.
weaknesses: Underlying attention memory bottleneck remains unaddressed: While DYPE adds zero overhead relative to standard model inference, generating at ultra-high resolutions ($4096^2$ and $6144^2$) remains heavily constrained by the quadratic scaling of full self-attention in DiTs; the paper would benefit from a clearer discussion on memory bounds or integration with memory-efficient attention / sequence parallelism.

Nuances in full-image FID at extreme resolutions: In Table 3 at $4096 \times 4096$, standalone DY-YaRN achieves an FID of 186.00, which is higher (worse) than HiFlow (174.39), although DY-YaRN achieves superior patch-level metrics (patch-FID 78.33 vs 78.38) and combining them yields the best overall score (169.46). Further discussion regarding global semantic consistency versus local patch fidelity at extreme scaling would provide valuable clarity.

Sensitivity to hyperparameters across diverse context scales: The scheduler introduces hyperparameters $\lambda_s$ and $\lambda_t$. While $\lambda_s=2, \lambda_t=2$ functions well across the evaluated setups, the extent to which these values generalize without tuning across vastly different aspect ratios or non-square resolutions could be analyzed more systematically.

strengths: Principled and intuitive motivation: The paper leverages the well-established low-to-high spectral progression of the diffusion process (low-frequency global structure settling early, high-frequency details settling late) to derive dynamic positional extrapolation schedulers.

Training-free and zero inference overhead: DyPE dynamically modifies rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) at each timestep during sampling without requiring fine-tuning, architecture modifications, or extra computational overhead beyond baseline generation.

Comprehensive empirical validation across backbones: The proposed dynamic scheduling is instantiated on Position Interpolation (DY-PI), NTK-aware interpolation (DY-NTK), and YaRN (DY-YaRN), and evaluated on both text-to-image (FLUX up to 4096×4096 and 6144×6144) and class-conditional generation (FiTv2 on ImageNet).

Solid qualitative and human evaluation results: Both visual comparisons and a 50-participant user study show marked improvements in structural coherence and textural detail over static baseline extrapolation methods (NTK-aware, YaRN).

Insightful contrast with prior work: The manuscript clearly explains and experimentally compares against Lumina-Next's time-aware RoPE (Table 4, Fig. 8), illustrating why relaxing toward base RoPE (uncompressed high frequencies) at late steps outperforms Lumina-Next's reverse interpolation schedule.
weaknesses: Heuristic nature of the dynamic scheduler: While the spectral analysis in Section 3.1 justifies shifting frequency emphasis over time, the exact parametric form of the scheduler $\kappa(t) = \lambda_s t^{\lambda_t}$ is largely empirical. The paper does not derive an analytical mapping from the progression map $\gamma(f, t)$ or the image PSD to the positional scaling factors.

Compute and memory feasibility at ultra-high resolutions: Generating 4096×4096 images with FLUX corresponds to approximately 65,536 sequence tokens. The paper notes running experiments on a single L40S GPU (Appendix C), but omits critical implementation details regarding attention memory management (e.g., whether RingAttention, sequence parallelism, or specific memory-efficient flash attention kernels were employed).

Statistical reliability of FID on Aesthetic-4K: The Aesthetic-4K evaluation set used for FID computation comprises only 195 image-prompt pairs, leading to unusually elevated FID values (~180–200). While relative differences are noticeable, drawing definitive conclusions on feature distributions from such small sample sizes is statistically noisy.

Missing comparisons to recent DiT-specific extrapolation works: Although the related work cites recent developments such as randomized positional encodings (Liu et al., 2025), direct empirical comparison against concurrent training-free extrapolation techniques specifically tailored for DiTs is absent.

Sensitivity to hyperparameters: The choice of $\lambda_s$ and $\lambda_t$ is tuned on a subset of 50 DrawBench prompts at 3072×3072. Further analysis is needed to assess how robust these specific choices are across different aspect ratios, steps (e.g., fewer-step distilled models), and guidance scales.

strengths: Principled and intuitive motivation: The paper grounds its method in a clear spectral analysis of the reverse diffusion trajectory, demonstrating that low-frequency content converges much earlier than high-frequency detail, which naturally justifies a time-varying positional encoding schedule.

Completely training-free and computationally lightweight: DYPE incurs no additional training or sampling compute overhead compared to standard inference, modifying only the positional frequency coordinates dynamically over timesteps.

Solid empirical gains across diverse resolutions and benchmarks: Extensive experiments on FLUX (up to 4096×4096 and 6144×6144) and FiTv2 show consistent quantitative (CLIPScore, ImageReward, Aesthetic Score, FID) and qualitative improvements over standard RoPE extrapolation baselines (PI, NTK-aware, YaRN).

Thorough ablations and comparisons: The paper systematically explores scheduler parameterizations (multiplicative vs. exponential, scheduler progression exponents) and clarifies the conceptual differences and empirical advantages over Lumina-Next's inverted time-aware scaling.
weaknesses: Incomplete editorial details and placeholders: The paper contains unfinished placeholder entries, such as 'Project page is available at' in the abstract and 'Placeholder YourTeam. Fit v2...' in the references list.

Limited exploration of larger extrapolation factors on class-conditional benchmarks: While FLUX is tested up to 4× linear resolution (4096×4096 from 1024×1024), the FiTv2 experiments on ImageNet only test modest extrapolation (from 256×256 up to 384×384, a 1.5× linear increase). Testing larger resolutions on FiTv2 would strengthen the generality of the method across architectures.

Lack of wall-clock time and memory footprint discussion: While DYPE does not introduce extra computation beyond standard inference at a given resolution, generating 4096×4096 images on full DiT attention remains memory- and compute-intensive. A brief discussion of practical hardware memory requirements, attention optimizations (e.g., FlashAttention/ring attention), and latency would be valuable.

strengths: Principled and intuitive motivation: The core hypothesis—that diffusion models resolve low-frequency macro-structures early and refine high-frequency details later—is well substantiated via Fourier-space analysis of the intermediate diffusion distributions. Linking this spectral trajectory directly to dynamic positional encoding extrapolation is original and elegant.

Training-free with negligible overhead: DYPE requires no fine-tuning or retraining of existing models and introduces virtually zero computational overhead during inference, altering only the time-dependent positional encoding coordinates and frequency scales.

Strong and consistent empirical performance: Extensive experiments across text-to-image (FLUX up to 4096×4096 and 6144×6144) and class-conditional generation (FiTv2 on ImageNet) show clear gains over static RoPE extrapolation schemes (PI, NTK-aware, YaRN) and prior dynamic approaches (Lumina-Next) in CLIPScore, ImageReward, aesthetics, and human preference.

Thorough ablation study: The ablation section clearly examines scheduler formulations (exponential vs. multiplicative, values of exponents and multipliers) and validates why modulating the YaRN ramp thresholds outperforms alternatives.
weaknesses: Discussion of hardware memory and attention scaling at ultra-high resolutions is limited: At 4096×4096 resolution, the latent grid produces tens of thousands of tokens, incurring quadratic attention compute and large memory footprints. While DYPE does not add overhead relative to baseline inference at that resolution, practical details on memory management (e.g., FlashAttention, ring attention, or tiling) and actual sampling wall-clock times are omitted.

Statistical reliability of distributional metrics on small prompt sets: The FID reported on the Aesthetic-4K benchmark is calculated over a relatively small set (195 images/prompts), where Fréchet inception distances typically exhibit high variance and may not reliably reflect true feature distribution alignment.

Evaluation on broader text-to-image DiT architectures: The ultra-high-resolution text-to-image experiments focus predominantly on FLUX.1. Evaluating additional open-source DiT architectures (e.g., PixArt-Sigma, SD3) would further substantiate the universality of the proposed time-dependent extrapolation formula across different DiT implementations.
Minor presentation polish: On page 1, the project page link is left blank ("Project page is available at"), and page 15 contains an unedited placeholder entry ("Placeholder YourTeam").
